title: The Fox and the Cat

full_text:
A proud, boastful fox met a humble grey cat wandering along a woodland trail. Looking down his slender snout at the little feline, the fox puffed his chest and said arrogantly: "Good day, mistress cat! How can a poor, ordinary creature like you survive in these perilous woods where hounds and hunters roam?"

"I manage well enough," purred the cat modestly. "I know only one single trick, but it has never failed me."

"Only one trick?" laughed the fox with uproarious scorn. "How pitiful! I am the undisputed master of a hundred cunning strategies! I possess an entire bag full of brilliant wiles—I can double back on my trail, swim beneath water reeds, blend with autumn foliage, and baffle the keenest hounds in the kingdom!"

Just at that moment, the baying of a ferocious pack of hunting hounds shattered the forest quiet, accompanied by the blast of hunting horns and galloping hooves.

In an instant, the cat executed her one trick: she sprang gracefully up the rough bark of a tall beech tree, perching safely among the highest leafy boughs where no hound could ever reach.

"Quick, Master Fox!" called the cat from above. "Open your bag of a hundred tricks! Choose your best strategy!"

The bewildered fox darted left, sprinted right, doubled back, crawled into a briar patch, and attempted twenty clever schemes at once. But in his frantic indecision and panic, the hounds encircled him, cutting off every escape until he was caught.

Watching from her secure perch, the cat sighed: "A hundred brilliant theories are worthless when danger strikes, while one simple, practical defense preserves life and limb."
moral: One safe and reliable plan is better than a hundred brilliant schemes that fail in peril.
